reconstruction.scope: Standing Temple of the Moon heritage compound: mapped red double-eaved green-roofed bell tower with real ground arch and recessed upper lattice, mapped triple-arched roofed park gate with open center/closed side leaves, and mapped west hall with swept green roof/red lattice doors. Include approximate surviving gray inner enclosure/three blocked pale Lingxing portals and short mapped northern outer-wall runs. Original simplified painted-beam/ridge/finial vocabulary, no copied text/photo atlas. Do not reconstruct the no-longer-intact altar. Modern lattice transmission mast and southern park landscaping/pavilions remain host context, not part of this heritage-building model.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Ordinary-picture/map estimates: bell tower upper roof reaches about15m above its local floor; ground arch3.8m wide/5.4m tall, lower red chamber6.0m, upper chamber from7.0m to10.9m, two green roofs. Gate eave6.7m/ridge9.8m with three approximately4.2m wide arches. West hall eave4.5m/ridge7.3m and six lattice door panels. Lingxing center stone portal5.5m high, sides4.8m, gray blocked panels2.9m; inner wall3m high, short red outer walls3.2m. Absolute heights, painted/roof/door inventories, inner enclosure dimensions and hidden rooms remain approximate.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Retain original pinned standard6m Mapzen ground, native park paths/water and all independent buildings. Each occupied building uses a level floor just above its sampled roof-envelope ground maximum, individually buried footing and narrow graded approaches. Enclosure footings/coping follow the sampled ground. No broad park slab, terrain flattening, water/ground cutout or invented reconstructed altar platform. Coarse DEM cannot resolve paving/door thresholds; absolute floor levels remain approximate.
